subject: Urgent: HyperNova retry cascade — dedicated pool saturation
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon@hypernova.ai>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: ops@hypernova.ai
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production timeouts + 5xx spike (started 08:55 PDT)

Hi team,

We started seeing a large number of timeouts and 5xx errors against the API around 08:55 PDT. Our product is returning 5xx for many user requests and some calls are timing out at the client after retry loops. We rely on your Dedicated pool (rdw-dedicated-hypernova) for peak inference. Latency has jumped from 120ms p50 to 2.3s p50 and 5xx rate is ~8% on the last 30m. This is causing major customer impact (signup flow and chat sessions dropping).

We attached the request-level logs and a short Kibana extract. Can you confirm:
- What's the current pool utilization?
- Any autoscale activity or failed scale events?
- Is there a recommended immediate mitigation while you investigate?

We are putting an incident banner on our status page. Please escalate — our CTO is on standby.

Thanks,
Simon
CTO, HyperNova

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@hypernova.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts + 5xx spike (started 08:55 PDT)

Simon — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs, we see the same in our telemetry. I am escalating this immediately to SE and Ops. Initial observations: theres a sudden queue buildup on the dedicated pool and autoscale events show multiple failed attempts to add nodes between 08:50 and 09:05 PDT. That aligns with GPU exhaustion causing model inference to fail with 5xx and some timeouts in the request path.

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Triggering manual warm-up + emergency burst capacity for rdw-dedicated-hypernova (ETA 6-8 minutes).
- Disabling the aggressive retry policy for that customer route to reduce cascading retries (we can do a per-route override).
- Asking SE (Ben) to gather kernel/oom traces and prefix cache stats; copying logs to shared Drive.

We will keep you updated every 15 minutes. I will also pull together a credits/comp plan and timeline for a short-term capacity increase.

Apologies for the disruption — were treating this as high-priority.

— Soojin
Support Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Benjamin Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Simon Park <simon@hypernova.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts + 5xx spike (started 08:55 PDT)

On Mon, Apr 1, 2028 at 09:29 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Simon — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs, we see the same in our telemetry.

We pulled the kernel traces and GPU metrics. Findings so far:
- All nodes in the dedicated pool reached ~98-100% GPU mem for the model shard at the time of the spike.
- Autoscaler logs show an API rate limit error from the cloud provider when trying to provision additional nodes (x2 failed allocate events at 08:51 and 08:56).
- Prefix cache hit rate dropped sharply -> increased compute per request and longer KV cache warm-ups.
- Theres also a workload change from your side: a batch of long-context chat sessions started hitting the same model variant which amplified memory pressure.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- We enabled emergency burst (3 extra nodes) and routed new requests to a compatible lighter-weight model variant to reduce per-token memory. This reduced 5xx to ~1.6% within 10 minutes.
- We temporarily lowered the per-route max retries from 5 -> 1 to prevent retry amplification.

Next steps Im executing now:
- Collecting a detailed timeline and the failed-provision error codes for cloud support.
- Generating a suggested config: model quantization, smaller batch size, and a routing rule to fallback to a lower-memory model when prefix cache miss rate > 30%.

Ill upload the raw traces to the Drive link and send a short runbook for your SREs.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pool-utilization-snapshot-0900.png (image)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Park <simon@hypernova.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts + 5xx spike (started 08:55 PDT)

Folks — looping in leadership to confirm executive visibility and a compensation path. Simon, Im sorry about the impact here. Please confirm whether a 4-hour SLA credit and a short-term Dedicated capacity bump (2x for 48 hours) would suffice while we implement the mitigations Ben recommended.

Internal ask for ops/product: take the failed-provisioning pattern as a priority item. We need a hardening plan for autoscaler retries and provider rate-limit backoffs — this incident shows fragility. Ben, please include the exact cloud-rate-limit error strings in the incident packet.

I will prepare a one-page exec note for our CEO and CS leadership.

— Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@hypernova.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts + 5xx spike (started 08:55 PDT)

Simon — quick update and next steps after today's mitigation window.

Summary:
- Root cause (preliminary): Dedicated pool GPU exhaustion driven by simultaneous long-context sessions and a prefix-cache cold spike. Autoscaler attempts failed due to cloud provider rate limits; that prevented quick scale-up and led to retry amplification and 5xx bursts.
- Short-term remediation applied: emergency burst nodes, per-route retry limit override, fallback routing to a lower-memory model variant. Those actions reduced the 5xx rate to <0.5% and brought latency back toward typical ranges.

Compensation & follow-up:
- Marissa has proposed a 4-hour SLA credit and a 48-hour temporary capacity bump while we run a follow-up plan. I attached the draft SLA-credits-proposal.docx.
- Action items we will take in the coming week:
  1) Implement provider backoff/resilience for autoscaler (engineering) — owner: infra team, ETA 2 weeks.
  2) Add per-route fallback policy and automatic model-variant downgrade when prefix miss rate crosses threshold — owner: runtime/product, ETA 1 week for config, 3 weeks for rollout.
  3) Joint runbook session with HyperNova SREs to tune batching/quantization for your peak flows — schedule within 48 hours.

Please confirm acceptance of the credit + temporary bump and availability for the runbook session. We will keep monitoring and keep the channel open.

Thanks again for the rapid signals and patience.

— Soojin
Support Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: hypernova-logs-20280401.zip, SLA-credits-proposal.docx
